messages:
Noah: Hi folks  I'm preparing my first set of stacked PRs (a small runtime tweak + a follow-up doc update). Quick questions: do we prefer a single PR or multiple linked PRs? Also what's the recommended way to mark a PR as draft vs ready for review?

Zara: Congrats! For tiny changes (code + one doc) we usually keep them together. For anything that touches runtime hot paths vs docs, split them so reviewers can ignore the docs if they only care about perf.

Priya L: Draft PRs: click "Draft" when you want feedback but don't want merges. When ready, convert to "Ready for review". Add `WIP:` in the title is fine if you can't mark Draft for some reason.

Ben: Stacked PRs are fine when change depends on another commit. Use the PR description to link parents and put a short summary on each. Label the top PR `stack/top` and the follow-ups `stack/child`. Keeps CI noise lower.

Noah: Nice. Branch naming? We have `team/desc` and `feature/ISSUE-desc`—any preference for stacked PRs?

Zara: For stacks, include the issue number in the top branch e.g. `feature/ENG-900-stack-kv` and child branches `feature/ENG-900-part2` so it's obvious. Keep names short.

Priya L: Quick local checklist I run: `make lint`, `pytest tests/ -k fast`, and for runtime changes a tiny smoke with the local bench: `./bench/local_infer_bench.sh --iters 5`. If you touch serialization or config, run `python -m json.tool path/to/conf.json` to catch syntax issues.

Ben: Reviewers: check CODEOWNERS; for runtime ping @Ben or @Priya L. For docs-only ping @Zara. When in doubt, add one runtime and one docs reviewer.

Noah: Merge style? Squash or merge commit? What about co-authored commits?

Zara: Squash is preferred for small changes. If multiple people contributed and you need credit, use `Co-authored-by:` in the final commit body and squash. Keep the conventional commit prefix: `feat(runtime):` or `chore(docs):`.

Priya L: If CI flags a flaky test, add comment `CI: flaky` and tag @oncall-bot with the failing job id. The bot will suggest a rerun command.

oncall-bot: To re-run one job locally: `./scripts/ci_local_retry.sh <job>`; to rerun in GH Actions, click "Re-run jobs". If you believe the failure is infra, add `infra/ci` label and ping oncall.

Ben: Backports: only if the change is customer-facing or fixes a regression in stable. Add `needs-backport` label when you think it might be required. Release managers will triage.

Noah: Anything else for PR body content?

Priya L: Short template that reviewers love (paste it):
```
Summary: one line
Why: short motivation
Diff: key files changed
Testing: local steps + quick bench output
Risk: low/medium/high
Rollout: canary plan / metrics to monitor
```

Zara: And one nit: keep diffs under ~400 lines if possible. Smaller PRs = faster reviews and less churn.

Noah: Perfect 2 I'll split the docs only if needed, mark the stack branches clearly, run lint+fast tests and the tiny bench, and ping @Ben + @Priya L when ready. Thanks all :raised_hands:
